standard.title: Initiate and sustain exchanges in familiar and unfamiliar contexts
standard.description: initiate and sustain exchanges in familiar and unfamiliar contexts related to students' experiences, feelings and views, adjusting their language in response to others
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can initiate and sustain exchanges related to experiences and perspectives, using active listening strategies and opinion-sharing language (AC9LCH6C01). They can sustain face-to-face and digital exchanges. They have not yet adjusted language in real-time response to others, sustained exchanges in genuinely unfamiliar contexts, used descriptive and persuasive language to discuss contrasting perspectives, or summarised others' views in interaction.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students initiate and sustain exchanges in familiar and unfamiliar contexts about their experiences, feelings and views, adjusting their language in response to others and demonstrating active, responsive listening.

nodes.label: Sustaining exchanges in unfamiliar contexts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can sustain an exchange in an unfamiliar or open-ended context — on topics beyond scripted school and home content — using strategies to maintain conversation when language resources are stretched.
nodes.minimum_width: Sustain an exchange for at least five turns on a topic that is partially or fully unfamiliar, using at least one strategy (clarification, paraphrase, or follow-up question) when language resources are insufficient.
nodes.typical_width: Sustain face-to-face and online exchanges in familiar and some unfamiliar contexts; use open-ended questions to maintain conversation; use clarification, repetition and paraphrase strategies; use descriptive language to discuss contrasting perspectives on personal topics; contribute to online forums and discussions.
wider: Sustain an exchange on a topic introduced spontaneously by the partner — demonstrate real-time adaptation to an unplanned topic direction across at least six turns
Participate in an online or written forum exchange where the topic and participants are partially unfamiliar — sustain contribution across multiple turns
nodes.hinge_reason: Sustaining exchanges in unfamiliar contexts is the prerequisite for all higher-order interaction work. Students who can only manage scripted or familiar exchanges cannot meet the 'adjusting language in response to others' demand or develop the interactional flexibility that the Y9-10 descriptors require.

response_modes.reason: Conversational resilience in unfamiliar contexts is built through accumulated experience across varied topics and partners. Structured practice with progressively less familiar topics — combined with explicit strategy instruction for when language resources run short — builds the confidence and flexibility the descriptor requires.

success_criteria: Sustains an exchange for at least five turns in a partially unfamiliar context
Uses at least one maintenance strategy (clarification, paraphrase, or follow-up question) when needed

nodes.label: Acknowledging views and using persuasive language
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can acknowledge others' ideas, indicate agreement or disagreement non-judgementally, and use language to persuade or influence others during an exchange.
nodes.minimum_width: Use at least two strategies for acknowledging or responding to others' views (agreement, qualified disagreement, or persuasive language) during a sustained exchange.
nodes.typical_width: Acknowledge others' ideas and indicate positions non-judgementally; use persuasive and influencing language including consequence-framing and perspective-offering; express views on contrasting aspects of personal experience — home/school, study/leisure; contribute personal ideas to discussions.
wider: Participate in a structured debate or discussion where views must be defended under challenge — demonstrate the use of persuasive language and reasoned position-holding
Compare how persuasive and influencing language is used differently in target language and English conversational contexts — identify where the conventions diverge

response_modes.reason: Acknowledgement and persuasive language must function across varied discussion contexts — peer exchange, group discussion, online forum — before they transfer reliably. Practising across different interaction formats and partner types builds flexible deployment.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Persuasive and influencing language in the target language is a marker of genuine communicative maturity. Background learners who can negotiate and persuade in their home language have a model for this capacity — width investment here builds the transfer of this capability to the target language school context.
success_criteria: Uses at least two strategies for acknowledging or responding to others' views during a sustained exchange
Produces at least one instance of persuasive or influencing language (e.g. framing consequences, offering perspective)

nodes.label: Real-time language adjustment
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can adjust their language in real-time in response to others — summarising views, rephrasing for clarity, or shifting register — as an exchange develops.
nodes.minimum_width: Demonstrate at least one instance of real-time language adjustment in a sustained exchange — for example, rephrasing after a signal of non-understanding, summarising a peer's view, or shifting register in response to context.
nodes.typical_width: Adjust language in response to interlocutor signals — rephrasing, simplifying, shifting register; summarise different opinions in interactions; request and provide clarification; use digital technology to maintain contact and extend exchanges across time and context.
wider: Reflect on a recorded exchange and identify every moment where language adjustment was or should have been made — discuss what triggered or should have triggered each adjustment
Practise summarising a peer's view accurately during a discussion — then compare the summary with the peer's intended meaning and discuss any gaps

response_modes.reason: Real-time language adjustment integrates unfamiliar context resilience (node 1) and acknowledgement/persuasion (node 2) into the full interaction demand of the descriptor. The teaching investment is in live interaction conditions — not pre-planned exchanges — that require genuine real-time responsiveness.

success_criteria: Demonstrates at least one instance of real-time language adjustment during an unprompted exchange
Can identify what triggered the adjustment and explain the choice made
